title: WHAT IF THE EARTH STOPPED SPINNING?
hook_text:
WHAT IF THE
EARTH STOPPED
SPINNING?
voice_style: Deep, calm male documentary narrator (ElevenLabs Adam/Brian), stability ~50%.
display: sixteen hundred and seventy kilometers per hour

segments.heading: BUT YOU DIDN'T
segments.text: The ground stopped. But you didn't.

segments.heading: THROWN EAST
segments.text: On the equator, you're thrown east at sixteen hundred and seventy kilometers per hour.

segments.heading: THE AIR KEEPS GOING
segments.text: So does the air. Winds three times stronger than the worst tornado ever measured.

segments.heading: SAFER AT THE POLES
segments.text: But near the poles, that speed shrinks. At the pole itself, you'd barely move.

segments.heading: A NEW SUPERCONTINENT
segments.text: Then the oceans drain toward the poles, leaving one giant continent around the middle.
segments.event: Esri/Fraczek: ~8 km water bulge migrates; equatorial megacontinent.

segments.heading: 1 DAY = 1 YEAR
segments.text: And one day would last a whole year. Six months of daylight. Six months of night.

segments.heading: 70 MILLION YEARS AGO
segments.text: The good news? Earth can't just stop. But it is slowing down. When dinosaurs lived, a day was only twenty-three and a half hours.
segments.event: de Winter et al. 2020, rudist shell.
